rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a multimodal baseline to establish whether combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses pca_n2000 (a standard RNA encoder) and resnet50 (a standard image encoder) with simple concatenation fusion, which is a logical starting point to assess the value of multimodal integration without overcomplicating the design. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches are worth pursuing before exploring more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000+resnet50, concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) improves performance, clarifying the importance of fusion strategies. It directly builds on the previous configuration, maintaining other parameters to isolate the effect of fusion type, which is a critical design decision with potential for significant performance impact.

The existing evidence shows that for singleprofile multimodal models with pca_n2000 and resnet50, concat fusion slightly outperforms weighted fusion (0.526 vs 0.523 accuracy). However, multiprofile settings have not been tested yet. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which will clarify whether multiprofile settings can improve performance and whether aggregation methods matter. It directly addresses a key design choice (profile setting and aggregation) with high potential impact.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups (config_018) achieve significantly higher accuracy (0.6186) than singleprofile ones. This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat to weighted (used in config_017) could further improve performance in the multiprofile context. It directly builds on the strong foundation of config_018 while exploring a critical design choice (fusion method) that may have a meaningful impact.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve high validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (config_031) further improves performance while keeping the high-performing aggregation/fusion setup. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice in multimodal settings, leveraging strong prior evidence to explore a critical design decision.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder and switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer, which could further improve performance. It directly extends the promising direction of config_031 by exploring critical design choices (image encoder and aggregation method) that may have large impact, balancing exploitation of current leads with exploration of key uncertainties.

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and scvi_n200 RNA (config_039) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt RNA encoder maintains or improves performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice in multimodal multiprofile settings.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (as in config_039) yields high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the scvi_n200 RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (a simpler model) maintains this performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder complexity. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of RNA encoder choices, which remains a key uncertainty.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile setups with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could clarify if RNA encoder choice (scgpt vs scvi_n200) impacts performance when using transformer aggregation. It addresses an important design choice (RNA encoder) while maintaining other high-performing components.

Existing evidence shows high performance with multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, and imagenet_vit_l (config_039). This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and concat fusion (vs scgpt and weighted fusion) maintains high performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder and fusion type. It balances exploitation of high-performing components with exploration of alternative design choices.
